claim: vLLM Router's basic and standard usage documentation is entirely static-worker-URL-based ('--worker-urls http://worker1:8000 http://worker2:8000'); Kubernetes Service Discovery is a separate, opt-in feature documented under 'Advanced Features,' not the default operating mode.
stance_target: leading non-K8s router alternatives to llm-d are static-URL-first by design, with K8s discovery as an add-on
scope_conditions: vllm-project/router README, HEAD as of Sept 2026
quoted_support: Launch router with data parallelism (8 replicas per worker URL) ... --worker-urls http://worker1:8000 http://worker2:8000 --policy consistent_hash ... ### Kubernetes Service Discovery\nAutomatic worker discovery and management in Kubernetes environments.

claim: vLLM Router supports three distinct, Kubernetes-independent backend-discovery mechanisms for prefill/decode disaggregation depending on the KV transfer connector in use: static CLI-supplied URL lists (NIXL connector), a ZMQ-based discovery endpoint (NCCL connector, via --vllm-discovery-address), and router-initiated queries to each prefill node's Mooncake bootstrap server at startup (Mooncake connector).
stance_target: production-grade routers already implement multiple non-K8s worker-discovery strategies for disaggregated serving
quoted_support: When vLLM runs the Mooncake connector, pass --kv-connector mooncake. The router queries each prefill node's Mooncake bootstrap server at startup to learn engine_id per DP rank, and injects transfer_id / remote_bootstrap_addr / remote_engine_id into each request's kv_transfer_params for P/D coordination.

claim: Load-balancing policies (cache-aware, power-of-two, consistent hashing, random, round robin) in vLLM Router are configured via a separate --policy flag independent of the worker-discovery mechanism (static URLs, K8s selectors, ZMQ, or Mooncake bootstrap), confirming routing-policy and discovery are architecturally decoupled in this codebase.
stance_target: existing routers already decouple routing-policy code from the backend-discovery layer, which is the architectural pattern the user would need to replicate for a non-K8s llm-d-derived router
scope_conditions: vllm-project/router CLI flags, README usage examples
